title: Phase 2: Key Validation Contract Test for analytics skill
outcome: Created test_contract.py with 24 contract tests validating key alignment between merge.py output and consumers (render_consolidated_report.py, charts.py). All 145 tests pass (121 existing + 24 new).
key_decisions: Used merge_datasets() with representative test data as the canonical fixture instead of a static JSON file, ensuring the contract test always validates against actual merge.py behavior
Chose static source analysis (regex extraction of .get('key') calls) for renderer/charts validation, avoiding the need to mock or instrument the rendering functions
Included negative tests (TestContractDetectsMismatches) to verify the contract test itself is effective at catching key mismatches
Extracted _extract_get_keys to module level to eliminate duplication between TestRendererKeyConsumption and TestChartsKeyConsumption
learnings: Contract tests are preventative by nature — they pass when the code is correct but would fail if a future key rename breaks alignment
The merge.py output structure has 20+ top-level keys and each section has its own key schema; comprehensive coverage requires defining expected keys for all 10+ data sections
Static analysis of .get('key') patterns in source code is a practical approach for validating consumer-side key usage without runtime instrumentation
next_steps: Implement Phase 3: Date range and legacy sessions (meta.since/meta.until reflecting true project range)
Implement Phase 4: Security hardening of estimate_cache.py and UX tooltips for raw vs effective tokens
